summary: Iteration 19 — Phase 3 Founder Brief (degree-blind eligibility + precise licensure + 30d employer cap + velocity/lanes + credentials catalog + walk-ins + personas + supply-reality). Backend unit suites tests/test_gate_engine.py (23) + tests/test_phase3_safeguards.py (11) = 34/34 PASS in 0.19s. New live-preview integration file tests/test_phase3_integration_live.py = 13/14 PASS. The one failure surfaced a REAL BACKEND BUG in POST /api/v1/walkins (see backend_issues.critical below). Frontend: /feed page renders LaneTabs, SortSelector with the 3 required options, auto-suggests velocity sort when Income Now clicked, and shows the truthful empty state with the correct top-reasons + widen-prefs CTA. All P0 acceptance criteria met except (a) walkin duplicate-key crash and (b) missing data-testid on velocity/lane/distance chips.

critical.issue: Second (and every subsequent) walk-in for the same user returns HTTP 500 due to MongoDB DuplicateKeyError. Root cause: /app/backend/domains/walkin/__init__.py line 78-96 creates a companion applications row with job_id: None; the applications collection has a unique index uniq_open_app_per_user_job on (user_id, job_id) and Mongo treats missing/null job_id as a single key, so the 2nd insert collides. Reproduction: log in as fixture-ead@, POST /api/v1/walkins twice with distinct employers → first returns 200, second returns 500 with pymongo.errors.DuplicateKeyError 'dup key: { user_id: ..., job_id: null }'. Impact: (1) 429 walkin_rate_limited path is unreachable — server crashes on the 2nd request before rate limiter can trip; (2) any real user logging more than one walk-in per lifetime is blocked. Mitigation: change the index to partial ({unique:true, partialFilterExpression:{job_id:{$type:'string'}}}) so null job_id rows are excluded, OR generate a per-walkin synthetic job_id string like 'walkin:<uuid>' when inserting the companion application row (line 81 in walkin/__init__.py). Recommend the partial-index approach so it doesn't leak into other producers of job_id-less applications.

ui_bugs.issue: The three chips required by the review request are rendered visually (e.g. '~$2,500/wk' badge for velocity.weekly_est_usd=2500) but carry NO data-testid attributes, so automated tests cannot assert their presence. Recommend adding data-testid='job-card-velocity-chip', 'job-card-lane-chip', 'job-card-distance-chip' on the corresponding <Badge/> nodes in frontend/src/pages/Feed.jsx JobCard component.

feed-empty-try-income is documented in the review request as a button on the empty state; on Income Now lane the button is (correctly) absent because the user is already in Income Now. Behavior matches spec ('if not already in it'), noting for completeness — not a bug.

Could not verify in-situ: the fixture user's approved education (MS ME) + employment (~5.5 yrs) exceeds SampleCo requirements so every passing card returns notes=[] from the API. Backend gate-engine correctly emits notes (verified in unit tests test_only_three_hard_gate_families_can_fail + test_evaluate_returns_notes_list). To confirm frontend NotesList rendering, either add a SampleCo seed with a legitimately queueable degree-mismatch or lower fixture education to BS temporarily. Non-blocking — data-driven, not a UI bug.

rca of the issue: POST /api/v1/walkins 500 RCA — code path: router.create_walkin() → when application_id is not provided it builds a companion applications doc with job_id:None (walkin/__init__.py:81) and calls db.applications.insert_one(app_doc). Mongo unique index uniq_open_app_per_user_job on (user_id, job_id) treats absent/null job_id values as equal, so the second walk-in per user violates the uniqueness constraint and pymongo raises DuplicateKeyError → FastAPI translates to HTTP 500. Reproduced deterministically 6 times in a row (all 500). Fix options in order of preference: (1) drop and recreate the index with partialFilterExpression:{job_id:{$type:'string'}} so null-job_id rows are exempt from uniqueness; (2) synthesize job_id=f'walkin:{uuid.uuid4()}' in the companion app_doc so each walk-in has a unique key; (3) skip the companion applications insert entirely for walk-ins and let the walkins collection stand alone. Option (1) is safest because it preserves the invariant for real posting-linked applications while allowing walk-ins.
